sections.h2: City gas passed fertiliser as India's top gas consumer in Q1 FY2026-27

chart.title: City gas led fertiliser in the quarter, 4,964 to 4,703 MMSCM
chart.source: PPAC, Natural Gas Current-Year Sectoral Consumption workbook (NG-C), provisional.

sections.means: City gas was ahead of fertiliser in each of April, May and June 2026, although one quarter is not yet a fiscal year.
sections.todo: Track the monthly city gas and fertiliser split through the Rabi season to see whether the lead holds.

sections.h2: City gas now takes 23.9% of India's gas, up from 11.4% in FY2015-16

chart.title: City gas is second only to fertiliser's 28.5% share of gas use
chart.sub: Share of total gas consumption, FY2025-26, %.
chart.source: PPAC, Natural Gas Historical Sectoral Consumption workbook (NG-H), provisional.

sections.means: City gas's share rose from 11.4% to 23.9% over the decade, while power's share fell from 22.8% to 11.5%.
sections.todo: Publish the rule that allocates domestic gas between kitchens, vehicles and fertiliser plants, since city gas is now the largest lever on urban fuel bills.

sections.h2: Fertiliser burned more imported gas than city gas in June 2026, 1,446 against 850 MMSCM

chart.title: Fertiliser's June gas was 87% imported; city gas's was 49%
chart.sub: Imported LNG (RLNG) burned in June 2026, MMSCM.
chart.source: PPAC, Snapshot of India's Oil & Gas Data, July-26 edition; NG-C, provisional.

sections.means: Fertiliser's LNG exposure means every dollar on the LNG price flows through urea production cost into the fertiliser subsidy.
sections.todo: Budget the fertiliser subsidy against the LNG price, not only against the domestic gas allocation.
